children: A rise in Australia's unemployment rate in August to 4.6% was unexpected, but it won't stop the Reserve Bank of Australia from raising interest rate at next week's policy meeting. The RBA's senior staff have gone to a lot of effort in recent weeks to pave the way for a further hike on Tuesday, all the while saying that a higher jobless rate might be needed to curb demand. The RBA has also played down concerns that house prices will fall at an even faster pace. The inflation worries of the RBA are real and appear to have deepened after recent global central bank meetings in the U.S. (james.glynn@wsj.com; @JamesGlynnWSJ)
